data.name: Nagarajan
data.gender_notes: Nagarajan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nagarajan is a name derived from the Sanskrit language, meaning 'King of Serpents'. This powerful and majestic name is believed to bring protection, courage, and wisdom. It is also associated with the Hindu deity Nagaraja, who is the king of all serpents and the lord of the underworld. The name Nagarajan carries the meaning “King of Serpents” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada. Parents who choose Nagarajan usually hope their child will grow to embody king of serpents and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Nagarajan is a divine name that represents the spiritual power of protection and wisdom. It is believed to bring blessings and prosperity to those who carry this name.
data.etymology: Nagarajan belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “King of Serpents.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nagarajan total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Nagarajan was a prominent Chola warrior and commander during the reign of Rajaraja Chola I (985-1014 CE). He is believed to have played a significant role in the expansion of the Chola empire, particularly in the southern and eastern regions.

Nagarajan is also mentioned in the 13th century Tamil epic 'Silapathikaram' as a wealthy and influential person in the city of Madurai during the Sangam period (approximately 200 BCE to 300 CE). He is known for his generosity and his patronage of art and literature.
